chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the woman when she dies and there is no woman with her to wash her, he said: Her husband inserts his hand under her shirt and washes her up to the elbows.

key_terms.تُغَسِّلُهَا: to wash her (ritual bathing of the deceased)

ai.seo_question: How does a husband wash his deceased wife if no other women are present?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific protocol for spousal washing (ghusl al-mayyit) when female relatives are absent, emphasizing the husband's role as the primary caretaker. The detail of inserting the hand under the garment (qamis) highlights the balance between ritual purity and maintaining modesty (haya), a key principle in Shia fiqh regarding the exposure of awrah during burial rites.
